schema_note: Per-function protection status for the Factory's customer-facing generators and shared systems. Seeded 2026-09-12 from a read-only audit -- see PROTECTED_GENERATOR_RULE.md and SESSION_HANDOFF_2026-09-11.md. Status values: LOCKED (proven customer-path fix + machine-checked protected test(s) + known last_known_good_commit), UNLOCKED (an explicit, reasoned, in-progress exception -- see unlocked_by/unlocked_reason), PROTECTED (real test coverage exists but no single commit has been proven as its customer-path last-known-good), UNPROTECTED (no meaningful customer-path test coverage), REGRESSION (currently known broken). last_known_good_commit is null unless a real commit was proven -- never manufactured (Rule 9, PROTECTED_GENERATOR_RULE.md). shared_code_dependencies covers both the function's own dedicated files and any file it shares with other functions -- tests/test_function_lock_enforcement.py treats a trailing '/' as a directory-prefix match.

ebook.notes: Largest test family in the Factory (~31 files in tests/acceptance_manifest.json), but only 1-2 run in the Fast Gate. No single commit has been formally proven as this function's customer-path last-known-good -- not LOCKED until one is. 2026-09-12: added the Global Cover Policy files -- Ebook's cover is the primary product this policy applies to, and it also has its own separate guided Pexels/upload cover system (ebook_photo_cover.py/ebook_pexels.py) which shares Pexels infrastructure with cover_source_policy.py. 2026-09-13: added services/ebook_build_orchestrator.py, services/ebook_project_workspace.py and services/ebook_manuscript_engine.py -- the One-Click Build state machine and its resume/idempotency logic -- as real, previously-undeclared shared dependencies; a live production build got stuck at a 'Try again' dead end because of two bugs in this exact code, fixed this session (see tests/test_ebook_build_resume_recovery.py). 2026-09-13 (recovery sprint): added services/ai_providers.py and services/ebook.py -- after the Resume Build fix, the live manuscript stage still failed every time with 'Connection refused' to 127.0.0.1:11434 (the owner's local Ollama). A first fix (v1.7.7) added routes_local()'s _running_on_render(), refusing local routing whenever an assumed Render-auto-injected RENDER variable was present -- a brand-new live build after that fix deployed hit the identical failure, proving that signal was not reliably present in the actual runtime. Corrected in v1.7.8: DEFAULT_POLICY changed from local-first to premium -- local generation is opt-in ONLY (FACTORY_AI_POLICY must be explicitly set), so a missing/wrong/dropped setting means cloud on any hosting platform, with nothing left to detect; _running_on_render() was removed entirely (see tests/test_ai_provider_render_safety.py, rewritten for this contract). 2026-09-13 (recovery sprint, part 3): the provider-routing fix held on the next live build, which then failed at manuscript QA/approval instead -- 'Resolve structural/content findings...' then, on retry, 'Cannot approve an empty manuscript.' Root cause, found by direct trace: services/ebook_build_orchestrator.py::_run_manuscript called approve_stage() directly after generation, which is guaranteed to raise when the stage needs correction, without ever using the Factory's existing execute_correct_manuscript() correction system; and advance_build()'s exception handler persisted the STALE pre-attempt data snapshot on any failure, silently erasing whatever the runner had already saved (including the assembled manuscript) and forcing a full, re-billed regeneration on the next attempt. Fixed by wiring _run_manuscript to run the existing correction pass automatically once before approving, by persisting the assembled manuscript/QA state as an explicit checkpoint before approve_stage runs, and by having advance_build's exception handler re-read the database before recording a failure instead of overwriting it (see tests/test_ebook_manuscript_correction_recovery.py). Still PROTECTED, not LOCKED: no single commit had been proven as this function's customer-path last-known-good before any of these fixes, so this does not change that classification.
